title: prd-multitenant-sandbox-fidelity-control-and-audit-playbook-2026-08-30
author: Riley Chen
content:
Overview:

This PRD describes the product requirements and rollout playbook for a multitenant Sandbox offering focused on enforceable fidelity controls and end-to-end auditability for enterprise customers. The goal is to provide safe, low-friction discovery and integration environments (sandboxes) that preserve production fidelity constraints, prevent accidental cost overruns, and generate structured audit trails for security and compliance reviews.

Key objectives:
- Allow customers to create short-lived sandboxes that closely mirror production fidelity settings (model variants, quantization profiles, batching heuristics) while limiting cost exposure.
- Provide policy-driven fidelity controls that operators (customer admins and Redwood account teams) can configure and enforce per-tenant or per-sandbox.
- Emit tamper-evident audit logs for all fidelity, billing, and rollout actions tied to sandbox usage.
- Support seamless conversion of sandbox workloads to production deployments with preserved fidelity metadata to avoid regressions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: Sandbox creation API/console, fidelity constraint policy API, sandbox SLOs, billing caps and soft/hard budget enforcement, audit logging schema, onboarding checklist for enterprise customers.
- Out-of-scope: full production-grade autoscaling for sandbox clusters (we will reuse Dedicated burst pools), model training pipelines, and marketplace billing adjustments (handled in a follow-up ticket).

Success metrics (KRs):
- 90% of enterprise sandbox creations complete within 60s from API call in beta customers.
- Sandbox usage incurs <= 5% unexpected overages vs configured budget in the first 90 days.
- 100% of fidelity-affecting configuration changes in sandboxes produce structured audit entries and are queryable via the Console within 10s.
- Conversion-to-production flow used in at least 25% of onboarded enterprise trials within first 60 days.

SLOs and thresholds (applies to sandbox control plane operations):
- Sandbox create/delete API availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Fidelity policy evaluation latency (applied on request startup): p95 < 10ms.
- Audit log ingestion latency: p95 < 5s.

Functional requirements:
1) Sandbox lifecycle API and Console flows:
   - POST /v1/sandboxes: create sandbox with metadata {name, owner_id, tenant_id, fidelity_profile_id, budget_usd, ttl_hours, region}.
   - GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}: returns effective fidelity profile, budget usage, recent audit events.
   - Console wizard: guided creation with preflight fidelity compatibility check.

2) Fidelity policy model and enforcement:
   - Fidelity profiles are composable objects that include: model_variant (string), max_sequence_length (int), quantization_profile_id (string), batching_hint {max_batch_tokens, max_latency_ms}, token_generation_limits (tokens/minute), and allowed_functions list.
   - Policies can be scoped: tenant-default, team-override (requires admin approval), and sandbox-specific (must be subset of tenant-default).
   - Enforcement modes: soft (warnings + telemetry), hard (request rejection), and throttling (rate-limits applied with deterministic backoff).

3) Budgeting and billing controls:
   - Soft budget: 90% threshold emits alert to tenant admins and opens an internal support flag.
   - Hard budget: 100% threshold flips enforcement mode to hard; further requests are rejected until budget increased or TTL expires.
   - Billing reporting: daily aggregated CSV with fields {sandbox_id, tenant_id, day, tokens_consumed, est_cost_usd, fidelity_profile_id}.

4) Audit and compliance:
   - Every fidelity-modifying action (create/update/convert/override) must generate a structured audit entry with fields {timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, action, target_id, before_state_hash, after_state_hash, signed_by_service}.
   - Audit logs are retained per tenant for 90 days by default; enterprise customers may request 365-day retention as an add-on.
   - Audit log consumer API: GET /v1/audit?tenant_id=...&from=...&to=...&action=... with pagination.

5) Conversion and metadata preservation:
   - When a sandbox is promoted to production, the conversion API must capture: fidelity_profile_id, actual observed token distribution histogram, KV-cache warmup hints, and acceptance test results.
   - The promotion process produces a Promotion Report (JSON) stored in the tenant's project bucket and surfaced in Console.

Non-functional requirements:
- All policy decisions must be deterministic and replayable for the past 30 days (to support audits and billing disputes).
- Latency-sensitive enforcement must run in-process in the serving runtime for p95 request-path < 5ms added overhead.
- The control plane will validate fidelity profiles against a compatibility matrix (model family vs quantization profile vs hardware).

UX and Console flows:
- Sandbox quick-create: pre-populated defaults from tenant-default fidelity profile; optional guided mode to tweak batching/quantization.
- Budget warning toast + modal offering one-click temporary increase (requires approver flow).
- Audit view: filter by actor, action, fidelity field, and time range; deep link to raw log JSON and Promotion Reports.

APIs and example payloads (minimal):
- Create sandbox example:
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sandboxes" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '
  {
    "name": "payments-integration-staging",
    "owner_id": "user_6283",
    "tenant_id": "tenant_acme",
    "fidelity_profile_id": "fp-small-dialogue-quant8",
    "budget_usd": 500,
    "ttl_hours": 168,
    "region": "us-west-2"
  }'

- Audit log example (single entry):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-09-01T14:21:03Z",
    "actor_id": "user_6283",
    "actor_role": "tenant_admin",
    "action": "update_fidelity_profile",
    "target_id": "sandbox_92ab",
    "before_state_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
    "after_state_hash": "sha256:ef01...",
    "signed_by_service": "redwood-controlplane-v2"
  }

Acceptance criteria (must pass for GA):
- Automated integration test that simulates 1,000 concurrent sandbox starts across 100 tenants without exceeding controlled budgets and with audit logs present for each start.
- Console UI end-to-end test: create sandbox -> change fidelity profile -> observe audit entry -> promote to production -> verify Promotion Report generated and retained.
- Security review completed with no high-severity findings; encryption-at-rest for Promotion Reports and audit logs verified.

Rollout plan and milestones:
1) Beta (Q4 2026): 3 anchor enterprise customers; feature-flagged per-tenant; weekly health reviews; manual conversion support.
2) Early access (Q1 2027): 15 customers, console polish, budget enforcement automation, 90-day retention SLA offered.
3) GA (Q2 2027): public documentation, SDK support (Python/Node), subscription billing integration, 365-day retention as add-on.

Operational runbook (summary):
- On high-rate creation errors (>100 create failures / 5m): escalate to eng-platform oncall, toggle sandbox creation feature flag, run diagnostic: check control plane CPU/memory, policy-eval service logs (errors), and DB write latencies.
- For budget enforcement anomalies (customers report unexpected rejections): verify audit trail, check budget consumption pipeline lag, and manually approve temporary increases for impacted customers while engineering investigates.

Ownership and teams:
- Product lead: Riley Chen (owner for PRD)
- Engineering owners: eng-platform (sandbox APIs), eng-serving-runtime (in-process enforcement), eng-infra (billing pipeline and retention storage)
- Security & Compliance: owns audit schema approval and retention config
- Customer Success: onboarding checklist and 1:1 support for beta customers

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Customers may accidentally configure permissive sandbox fidelity leading to high costs. Mitigation: default sandbox profiles are conservative; hard budget enforcement is opt-in for trials and mandatory for public beta.
- Risk: Audit ingestion or query latency under heavy load. Mitigation: use a hot path to index essential fields and an archival pipeline for raw logs.

Open questions for review:
- Should sandbox budgets support mixed-currency billing natively or be limited to tenant currency for Q1?
- Should Promotion Reports include a signed digest that can be submitted as legal evidence during enterprise procurement reviews?

Appendix:
- Compatibility matrix (excerpt):
  Model family | Quantization profile | Supported regions | Notes
  ------------ | ------------------- | ----------------- | -----
  redwood-m1   | quant8-fast         | us-west-2, eu-west-1 | best-effort token parity with fp16
  redwood-m2   | quant4-high         | us-west-2           | only supported for <1024 seq len

- Sample alert policy (Console YAML):
  alert: sandbox_budget_warning
  when: budget_pct >= 90
  notify: [tenant_admins, cs_reps]

- Migration considerations: ensure historical fidelity metadata attached to requests for at least 30 days to diagnose early-conversion regressions.

This PRD is intended to be a living document during the in_review phase. Feedback from the reviewers above should be captured inline; major changes will be recorded in the rollout milestones and acceptance criteria.
